# Atelier — Mac Studio inference hub

LAN-only AI model server running on a Mac Studio (Apple M1 Max, 64 GB). Hosts production-grade ML inference workloads as Python sidecars so any client on the LAN (a SvelteKit webapp, a notebook, a CLI) can hit one HTTP endpoint per workload instead of running models in-browser.

**Codename: Atelier** (workshop). Internal-only.

## What runs here

| Sidecar | Port | Engine | Use case |
|---|---|---|---|
| `omnivoice` | 8770 | k2-fsa/OmniVoice (Diffusion LM, PyTorch MPS) | **PRIMARY TTS** — natural multi-speaker via instruct (accent/pitch/gender), ~0.6–1× RTF |
| `kokoro` | 8765 | kokoro-onnx (CoreML/MPS) | Fallback TTS — fast, fixed-voice library, ~0.6s/line (twin on Linux `:18765`) |
| `dia` | 8769 | nari-labs/Dia-1.6B-0626 (PyTorch MPS) | Expressive cloning TTS — **retired for live** (~10× RTF), overnight batch only |
| `comfyui` | 8188 | ComfyUI (PyTorch MPS) | Image + video generation. Wan2.1 1.3B + 14B Q4 verified |
| Ollama | 11434 | Apple's prebuilt | LLM serving (gemma, qwen3:32b, etc.) — managed outside Atelier but co-resident |

**Start here:** [`docs/ATELIER.md`](docs/ATELIER.md) — the full overview (what it is, how it
works, all media types, ambitions). Visual: [`docs/atelier-infographic.html`](docs/atelier-infographic.html).
Deep design: [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Topology — two boxes

Atelier is the **compute** half of a two-machine setup. It runs on the Mac; the
things that *consume* it run on a separate **Linux box**, over the LAN.

```
      Linux box (the Blade)                         Mac Studio · 192.168.0.159
      consumers / orchestration / UI                  "Atelier" · the compute

 │ Cl…

_**Agent (2026-05-30 09:38:57Z)**_

**Atelier** is a LAN-local AI inference server running on a Mac Studio (Apple M1 Max, 64 GB unified memory).

It hosts several ML sidecars as persistent HTTP services so any LAN client — a SvelteKit webapp, a notebook, a CLI — can hit a single endpoint per workload instead of running models directly.

**What it runs:**
- `omnivoice` (:8770) — primary TTS (multi-speaker, diffusion LM)
- `kokoro` (:8765) — fast fallback TTS
- `dia` (:8769) — expressive voice cloning (batch-only, retired from live)
- `comfyui` (:8188) — image/video generation (Wan2.1)
- `governor` (:8799) — memory management + ETA prediction
- Ollama (:11434) — LLM serving (co-resident but externally managed)

**Architecture:** two-box split — the Mac is the *compute hub* (models + GPU), a separate Linux machine (the Blade) is the *consumer* running the product UI (Radio Mode podcast webapp), orchestration, and agent tooling. They talk over HTTP on the LAN.

The project's main use case is an **AI-generated podcast** ("Radio Mode") where voice and content is produced on the Mac and consumed/orchestrated from the Linux box.

_**Agent (2026-05-30 10:56:46Z)**_

Yes — there's a fully drafted PRD for exactly that. It was removed from the repo and parked in an external `prd` system, but here's the gist:

**PRD — Atelier Native Dashboard (macOS / SwiftUI)**
Status: Draft, deferred (2026-05-26)

**What it would show** — real-time panels sourced from the governor + sidecar HTTP endpoints:

| Panel | What you see |
|---|---|
| **Memory pressure** (hero) | Live area chart of resident GB over time with WARN (45 GB) + CLIFF (55 GB) lines; big colored status pill (green/amber/red); swapout counter |
| **Tenants** (what's loaded) | One card per sidecar/model — state dot (idle/busy/cold), active jobs, queue depth, memory GB |
| **Inference flow** | Incoming req/min, outgoing tok/s (LLM) + audio-sec/s (TTS); rolling timeline of recent calls |
| **Per-class compute stats** | Bayesian tok/s rates per class (llm:thinking / large / standard, tts) visualized as bars |
| **Governor actions** | Last auto make-room + any pending force-stop recommendations as actionable cards |

**Tech:** SwiftUI + Swift Charts, macOS 14+, menu-bar item + full window, polling governor every ~2-3s, no auth (local only).

**Design language:** editorial / instrument-panel — dark, serif headers + monospace data, "financial terminal × oscilloscope" — not a Grafana template.

**Phases:**
1. Read-only pane of glass
2. Human-gated control surface (force-stop dialog, make-room button)
3. Persisted history + trend charts

So the answer is: yes, the design exists and is detailed. It just hasn't been built yet. Want to start on it?

Base directory for this skill: /Users/gyasisutton/.claude/skills/session-search

# session-search

Thin wrapper over `~/bin/session-search` — ripgrep across Claude Code JSONL session files.

## When to use

User signals past-work recall. Trigger phrases include:
- "did we talk about X"
- "remember when we"
- "I told you before"
- "what did we decide about Y"
- "where did we leave off"
- "last week / last time we"

For brand-new tasks: do NOT invoke. This is recall, not cold-start research.

## Usage cascade

1. **Scout with `--files`** — cheap, returns matching JSONL paths only.
   ```bash
   session-search "<3-6 keywords>" --files
   ```
2. **Read selectively** — `Read` the JSONL files that look promising. Each line is one event; conversation text is in the `text` field of user/assistant content.
3. **Widen only on miss** — `--recent 30` (default 7) or `--all` for historical. The recency-first gate is intentional.

## Other flags

- `--count` — matches per file (triage high-frequency terms)
- `--context N` — N lines around each match
- `--clean` — un-escape JSON for readable output
- `--specstory` — only formatted `.md` history. SpecStory is a Cursor/VSCode extension that writes to `<project>/.specstory/history/*.md`; the `claude` CLI does NOT populate it. On this Mac (claude-CLI only): **dead flag, returns nothing**. Don't reach for it.
- `--all` — JSONL + SpecStory + backups (effectively == JSONL + backups on this Mac)

## Failure mode

Clean "No matches" → state it and proceed cold. Don't widen blindly — three failed searches means the term isn't in the corpus.

## Why this exists

Anthropic's [Claude Design][cd] (released 2026-04-17, Opus 4.7) showed what happens when an LLM stops writing prose and starts shipping design artifacts. It went viral — and stayed closed-source, paid-only, cloud-only, locked to Anthropic's model and Anthropic's skills. There is no checkout, no self-host, no Vercel deploy, no swap-in-your-own-agent.

**Open Design (OD) is the open-source alternative.** Same loop, same artifact-first mental model, none of the lock-in. We don't ship an agent — the strongest coding agents already live on your laptop. We wire them into a skill-driven design workflow that runs on `pnpm dev`, deploys to Vercel, and stays BYOK at every layer.

# Quickstart

Run the full product locally.

## One-shot (dev mode)

```bash
nvm use                # uses Node 22 from .nvmrc
corepack enable
pnpm install
pnpm dev:all           # starts daemon (:7456) + Vite (:5173) together
open http://localhost:5173
```

On first load, the app detects your installed code-agent CLI (Claude Code / Codex / Gemini / OpenCode / Cursor Agent / Qwen), picks it automatically, and defaults to `web-prototype` skill + `Neutral Modern` design system. Type a prompt and hit **Send**. The agent streams into the left pane; the `<artifact>` tag is parsed out and the HTML renders live on the right. When it finishes, click **Save to disk** to persist the artifact under `./.od/artifacts/<timestamp>-<slug>/index.html`.

The **Design system** dropdown ships with 71 built-in systems — 2 hand-authored starters (Neutral Modern, Warm Editorial) and 69 product systems imported from [`awesome-design-md`](https://github.com/VoltAgent/awesome-design-md), grouped by category (AI & LLM, Developer Tools, Productivity, Backend, Design Tools, Fintech, E-Commerce, Media, Automotive). Pick one to skin every prototype in that brand's aesthetic.

The **Skill** dropdown groups by mode (Prototype / Deck / Template / Design system) and shows the default skill per mode with a `· default` suffix. Bundled skills:

- **Prototype** — `web-prototype` (generic), `saas-landing`, `dashboard`, `pricing-page`, `docs-page`, `blog-post`, `mobile-app`.
- **Deck / PPT** — `simple-deck` (single-file horizontal swipe) and `magazine-web-ppt` (the `guizang-ppt` bundle from [`op7418/guizang-ppt-skill`](https://github.com/op7418/guizang-ppt-skill) — default for deck mode, ships its own assets/template + 4 references). Skills with side files get an automatic "Skill root (absolute)" preamble so the agent can resolve `assets/template.html` and `references/*.md` against the real on-disk path instead of its CWD.

Pair a skill with a design system and a single prompt produces a layout-appropriate…

Yes — open **http://localhost:5173** in your browser, that's where the UI lives.

Here's exactly what to do once it's open:

1. **Skill** → select `dashboard`
2. **Design system** → select `linear-app` (dark, minimal, perfect for an inference hub)
3. **Paste this prompt:**

```
Atelier inference hub observability dashboard — dark editorial instrument-panel aesthetic.

LAYOUT:
- Top 70%: main dashboard area with 3 panels side-by-side (Memory | Tenants | Stats)
- Bottom 30%: fixed "Scene Info" HUD strip — always visible, always current

SCENE INFO HUD (bottom 30%):
- Left: PIE CHART — what's loaded right now (slices: omnivoice 18GB, kokoro 4GB, comfyui 12GB, ollama qwen3:32b 20GB, free 10GB). Label each slice with GB.
- Center: LINE GRAPHS stacked — (1) Time-to-First-Token in ms over last 20 requests, (2) tokens/sec generation speed over last 20 requests. Both with WARN threshold line.
- Right: STATUS TABLE — one row per sidecar: name | state dot (green up / amber busy / grey cold) | loaded since | TTFT avg | tokens generated total

MAIN PANELS (top 70%):
- Memory panel: area chart of resident_gb over time (60 samples), WARN line at 45GB, CLIFF line at 55GB in red, current value large in top-right
- Tenants panel: card grid — one card per model/sidecar showing state, active_jobs, queue_depth, mem_gb. Animate busy state with a subtle pulse.
- Task time-series panel: table (task name | start time | duration | status) PLUS a swimlane/gantt sparkline above it showing task activity as colored bars on a time axis (last 60 min)

_**Agent (2026-05-30 21:03:48Z)**_

Good question — here's the real tradeoff:

**The PRD already calls for SwiftUI** (that's what `tasks.md` is tracking). But now that we have the HTML prototype, a **Tauri** (Rust) approach is worth considering seriously.

| | Swift/SwiftUI | Tauri (Rust) |
|---|---|---|
| **UI** | Rebuild in Swift Charts from scratch | Reuse the HTML we just built — it's already done |
| **Menu bar** | Native `MenuBarExtra` | Native via Tauri plugin |
| **Polling** | `URLSession` actor | Rust `reqwest` + Tauri commands |
| **Design fidelity** | Re-implement every chart | Exact match — same HTML, Chart.js, live data |
| **Effort to Phase 1** | High — full rewrite in Swift | Low — wire real endpoints into existing HTML |
| **macOS feel** | Fully native | WebView (like VS Code, Linear) |
| **Chart quality** | Swift Charts (limited) | Chart.js (already tuned) |

**My take:** Tauri wins here. The HTML prototype is 90% of the UI work. The Rust backend just needs to:
1. Poll `127.0.0.1:8799/pressure`, `/telemetry`, `/predictor/stats`
2. Poll sidecar `/readyz` endpoints
3. Serve the data to the webview

You'd get the exact design you just approved, as a real `.app` with a menu bar item, in a fraction of the time.

Want me to update `tasks.md` to reflect a Tauri build instead of SwiftUI?

# Dev-Kid Orchestrate

Converts linear tasks.md into parallelized wave execution plan with dependency analysis.

## What This Does

1. Reads tasks.md (symlinked from .specify/specs/{branch}/tasks.md)
2. Analyzes file locks and dependencies
3. Creates execution_plan.json with PARALLEL_SWARM and SEQUENTIAL_MERGE waves
4. Reports wave structure

## Usage

```bash
/devkid.orchestrate
```

Or with custom phase name:

```bash
/devkid.orchestrate "Feature Implementation"
```

## Execution

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e

PHASE_NAME="${1:-Feature Implementation}"

# Check prerequisites
if [ ! -f "tasks.md" ]; then
    echo "❌ No tasks.md found"
    echo "   Run /speckit.tasks first or ensure tasks.md exists"
    exit 1
fi

# Get current branch
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo "main")

echo "🌊 Orchestrating tasks into execution waves..."
echo "   Phase: $PHASE_NAME"
echo "   Branch: $BRANCH"
echo ""

# Run orchestration
dev-kid orchestrate "$PHASE_NAME"

if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "✅ Execution plan created!"
    echo ""

    # Show wave summary
    if command -v jq &> /dev/null; then
        echo "📊 Wave Summary:"
        jq '.execution_plan.waves[] | "Wave \(.wave_id) (\(.strategy)): \(.tasks | length) tasks"' -r execution_plan.json
        echo ""
    fi

    echo "📋 Next steps:"
    echo "   1. Review: cat execution_plan.json"
    echo "   2. Execute: /devkid.execute"
else
    echo ""
    echo "❌ Orchestration failed"
    exit 1
fi
```

## Output

Creates `execution_plan.json` with structure:

```json
{
  "execution_plan": {
    "phase_id": "Feature Implementation",
    "waves": [
      {
        "wave_id": 1,
        "strategy": "PARALLEL_SWARM",
        "tasks": [...],
        "checkpoint_after": {...}
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Integration with Speckit

- Reads tasks from: `.specify/specs/{branch}/tasks.md` (via symlink)
- Extracts constitution rules embedded by /speckit.tasks
- Creates parallelized plan for /devkid.execute

# Dev-Kid Execute

Executes wave-based implementation plan with automatic checkpointing, constitution validation, and task monitoring.

## What This Does

1. **Preflight gate (built-in since dev-kid v2.1)** — Auto-sources `.env` from project root, runs `dev-kid sentinel-health`, presents an interactive menu if any provider is missing, and requires explicit y/N confirmation before any wave runs. Bypass with `--no-preflight` (advanced) or `--yes` for non-interactive CI.
2. Starts task watchdog for monitoring
3. Loads constitution rules
4. Executes waves sequentially (max 10 tasks per wave, configurable via dev-kid.yml wave_size)
5. At each wave checkpoint:
   a. Validates task completion ([x] markers in tasks.md)
   b. Integration Sentinel validates output (placeholder scan, micro-agent test loop, interface diff)
   c. Constitution compliance check
   d. Memory sync via `project-bank-keeper` agent
   e. Git checkpoint via `git-version-manager` agent
6. Reports PASS/FAIL/SKIP per task with tier info

**Recommendation**: Run `/devkid.init-check` once before your first `/devkid.execute` to validate setup.

## Usage

```bash
/devkid.execute
```

## Execution

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Check prerequisites
if [ ! -f "execution_plan.json" ]; then
    echo "❌ No execution_plan.json found"
    echo "   Run /devkid.orchestrate first"
    exit 1
fi

if [ ! -f "tasks.md" ]; then
    echo "❌ No tasks.md found"
    exit 1
fi

echo "🚀 Starting wave-based execution (preflight gate built-in)..."
echo ""

# Start watchdog
echo "🐕 Starting task watchdog..."
dev-kid watchdog-start
echo ""

# Load constitution if exists
if [ -f "memory-bank/shared/.constitution.md" ]; then
    echo "📜 Constitution loaded - rules will be enforced at checkpoints"
    echo ""
fi

# Execute waves — `dev-kid execute` now runs the preflight gate by default
# (auto-sources .env, sentinel-health, interactive y/N confirmation).
# Pass --no-preflight to bypass the gate, or --yes for non-interactive CI.
echo "🌊 Executing waves..."
echo ""
dev-kid execute

# Check execution result
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "✅ All waves executed!"
    echo ""
    echo "📋 Next steps:"
    echo "   1. Review changes: git status"
    echo "   2. Update memory: /devkid.sync-memory"
    echo "   3. Finalize session: dev-kid finalize"
else
    echo ""
    echo "❌ Wave execution failed"
    echo "   Check tasks.md for completion markers [x]"
    echo "   Review constitution violations if any"
    exit 1
fi
```

## Wave Execution Flow

```
Wave 1 (PARALLEL_SWARM, max 10 tasks)
  → Register tasks with watchdog
  → Execute tasks in parallel
  → Mark [x] in tasks.md as complete
  ↓
  [CHECKPOINT — automatic via wave_executor.py]
  → Verify all tasks have [x] markers
  → Integration Sentinel per task:
     • Placeholder scan (TODO/FIXME/stub detection)
     • Test loop via micro-agent (tiered: Ollama → Azure)
     • Interface diff (public API changes)
     • Change radius check (file/line budget)
  → Constitution compliance check
  → Memory sync (project-bank-keeper)
  → Git commit (git-version-manager)

Wave 2... (same pattern, automatic)
```

## Agent Delegation at Checkpoints

The execution_plan.json names specific Claude Code agents for checkpoint tasks:

| Agent | Role | Spawned when |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `project-bank-keeper` | Syncs progress.md, memory bank, activity stream | After wave validation passes |
| `git-version-manager` | Creates semantic git checkpoint | After memory sync + constitution check |

When using `dev-kid execute`, these are handled in-process.
When working manually, Claude should spawn these agents at wave boundaries.

## Sentinel Health Check

Before execution, verify providers are ready:

```bash
dev-kid sentinel-health
```

Shows per-tier readiness (Ollama models, Azure endpoints, API keys).
If any tier is unavailable, sentinel will SKIP (not false PASS) and report why.

## Constitution Enforcement

At each checkpoint, validates:
- ✅ Type hints present (if required)
- ✅ Docstrings present (if required)
- ✅ No hardcoded secrets
- ✅ Test coverage >80% (if required)
- ✅ No forbidden patterns

**Checkpoint BLOCKED if violations found.**

## Task Watchdog

Each task registered with:
- Task ID (T001, T002...)
- Command/instruction
- Constitution rules
- Start timestamp

Monitors:
- ⏱️ Task duration (7-minute guideline)
- 🚨 Stalled tasks (>15 min no activity)
- ✅ Completion detection (tasks.md [x] markers)

## Wave Resume

Execution automatically resumes from the first incomplete wave. If waves 1-3 are
already complete (all tasks marked `[x]`), execution starts at wave 4. No need to
manually skip completed waves.

## Configuration (dev-kid.yml)

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `wave_size` | 10 | Max tasks per wave (prevents monster waves) |
| `sentinel.enabled` | true | Enable/disable sentinel validation |
| `sentinel.test_command` | (auto-detect) | Override test command (e.g. `python -m pytest cli/`) |
| `sentinel.tiers_file` | ralph-tiers.json | Path to tier escalation config |
| `sentinel.min_tier` | (empty) | Skip tiers before this name (e.g. `azure-budget`) |

## Integration with Speckit

- Tasks from: `.specify/specs/{branch}/tasks.md`
- Constitution from: `memory-bank/shared/.constitution.md`
- Enforcement happens at wave boundaries

2000 },\n      { engine: 'qwen3:32b', chars: 890, output_tokens: 420, latency_s: 4.2, ts: Date.now() - 8000 },\n    ],\n    recent_synths: [\n      { chars: 840, seconds: 3.2, engine: 'omnivoice', ts: Date.now() - 1000 },\n      { chars: 620, seconds: 2.9, engine: 'omnivoice', ts: Date.now() - 5000 },\n    ],\n  };\n}\n\nexport async function fetchPredictorStats() {\n  const data = await invoke('get_predictor_stats');\n  if (data) return data;\n  return {\n    stats: [\n      { kind: 'llm', model: 'qwen3:32b',  runs: 142, avg_rate: 47.2, avg_seconds: 3.1 },\n      { kind: 'tts', model: 'omnivoice',  runs: 89,  avg_rate: 0.31, avg_seconds: 3.0 },\n      { kind: 'tts', model: 'kokoro',     runs: 34,  avg_rate: 0.18, avg_seconds: 2.2 },\n      { kind: 'img', model: 'wan2.1-1.3b',runs: 12,  avg_rate: 0.08, avg_seconds: 11.4 },\n    ],\n  };\n}\n\nexport async function fetchSidecars() {\n  const data = await invoke('get_sidecars');\n  if (data) return data;\n  return {\n    omnivoice: { lifecycle: 'running', active_jobs: 3, queue_depth: 7 },\n    kokoro:    { lifecycle: 'running', active_jobs: 0, queue_depth: 0 },\n    dia:       { lifecycle: 'stopped', active_jobs: 0, queue_depth: 0 },\n    comfyui:   { lifecycle: 'running', active_jobs: 1, queue_depth: 2 },\n    ollama:    { models: [{ name: 'qwen3:32b', size: 20000000000 }] },\n  };\n}\n"}

{"file_path":"/Users/gyasisutton/Documents/code/atelier/dashboard/src-tauri/src/fetcher.rs","content":"use reqwest::Client;\nuse crate::models::*;\n\nconst GOVERNOR: &str = \"http://127.0.0.1:8799\";\nconst OLLAMA:   &str = \"http://127.0.0.1:11434\";\nconst TIMEOUT:   u64 = 3; // seconds\n\nfn client() -> Client {\n    Client::builder()\n        .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(TIMEOUT))\n        .build()\n        .unwrap_or_default()\n}\n\npub async fn fetch_pressure() -> PressureResponse {\n    let c = client();\n    match c.get(format!(\"{GOVERNOR}/pressure\")).send().await {\n        Ok(r) => r.json::<PressureResponse>().await.unwrap_or_default(),\n        Err(_) => PressureResponse::default(),\n    }\n}\n\npub async fn fetch_telemetry() -> TelemetryResponse {\n    let c = client();\n    match c.get(format!(\"{GOVERNOR}/telemetry\")).send().await {\n        Ok(r) => r.json::<TelemetryResponse>().await.unwrap_or_default(),\n        Err(_) => TelemetryResponse::default(),\n    }\n}\n\npub async fn fetch_predictor_stats() -> PredictorStatsResponse {\n    let c = client();\n    match c.get(format!(\"{GOVERNOR}/predictor/stats\")).send().await {\n        Ok(r) => r.json::<PredictorStatsResponse>().await.unwrap_or_default(),\n        Err(_) => PredictorStatsResponse::default(),\n    }\n}\n\npub async fn fetch_sidecar(port: u16) -> SidecarReadyz {\n    let c = client();\n    match c.get(format!(\"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/readyz\")).send().await {\n        Ok(r) => r.json::<SidecarReadyz>().await.unwrap_or_default(),\n        Err(_) => SidecarReadyz::default(),\n    }\n}\n\npub async fn fetch_ollama_ps() -> serde_json::Value {\n    let c = client();\n    match c.get(format!(\"{OLLAMA}/api/ps\")).send().await {\n        Ok(r) => r.json::<serde_json::Value>().await.unwrap_or(serde_json::json!({\"models\":[]})),\n        Err(_) => serde_json::json!({\"models\":[]}),\n    }\n}\n"}

{"file_path":"/Users/gyasisutton/Documents/code/atelier/dashboard/src-tauri/src/log_watcher.rs","content":"/// Tails launchd/stdout logs for Ollama, omnivoice, and comfyui.\n/// Parses token-rate, synth RTF, and image-progress lines into LogMetrics\n/// which the frontend polls via `get_log_metrics` command.\n///\n/// Log locations (Mac launchd stdout redirect):\n///   Ollama    : ~/Library/Logs/ollama.log  (or journald on Linux)\n///   omnivoice : ~/Library/Logs/omnivoice.log\n///   comfyui   : ~/Library/Logs/comfyui.log\n///\n/// Patterns extracted:\n///   Ollama    : \"... X tokens/s ...\"         → tokens_per_sec\n///   omnivoice : \"RTF: X.XX\"                 → synth_rtf\n///   comfyui   : \"Progress: XX%\"             → img_progress_pct\n\nuse std::collections::VecDeque;\nuse std::sync::Mutex;\nuse std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};\nuse crate::models::LogMetric;\n\nstatic METRICS: Mutex<VecDeque<LogMetric>> = Mutex::new(VecDeque::new());\nconst MAX_METRICS: usize = 120;\n\nfn now_ms() -> u64 {\n    SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or_default().as_millis() as u64\n}\n\nfn push(metric: LogMetric) {\n    if let Ok(mut q) = METRICS.lock() {\n        if q.len() >= MAX_METRICS {\n            q.pop_front();\n        }\n        q.push_back(metric);\n    }\n}\n\nfn log_path(name: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {\n    dirs_next::home_dir()\n        .unwrap_or_default()\n        .join(\"Library/Logs\")\n        .join(format!(\"{name}.log\"))\n}\n\n/// Parse a single log line and push a metric if it matches.\npub fn parse_line(source: &str, line: &str) {\n    match source {\n        \"ollama\" => {\n            // \"llama_print_timings: eval time ... X tokens/s\"\n            // or simpler: \"... 47.23 tokens/s ...\"\n            if let Some(pos) = line.find(\"tokens/s\") {\n                let before = &line[..pos];\n                if let Some(num_str) = before.split_whitespace().last() {\n                    if let Ok(v) = num_str.trim_matches(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit() && c != '.').parse::<f64>() {\n                        push(LogMetric { source: \"ollama\".into(), metric: \"tokens_per_sec\".into(), value: v, ts: now_ms() });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        \"omnivoice\" => {\n            // \"RTF: 0.62\" or \"real-time factor: 0.62\"\n            if let Some(pos) = line.to_lowercase().find(\"rtf:\") {\n                let after = &line[pos + 4..];\n                if let Some(num_str) = after.split_whitespace().next() {\n                    if let Ok(v) = num_str.trim().parse::<f64>() {\n                        push(LogMetric { source: \"omnivoice\".into(), metric: \"synth_rtf\".into(), value: v, ts: now_ms() });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        \"comfyui\" => {\n            // \"Progress: 45%\" or \"[45/100]\"\n            if let Some(pos) = line.find('[') {\n                if let Some(end) = line[pos..].find(']') {\n                    let inner = &line[pos+1..pos+end];\n                    let parts: Vec<&str> = inner.split('/').collect();\n                    if parts.len() == 2 {\n                        if let (Ok(cur), Ok(tot)) = (parts[0].trim().parse::<f64>(), parts[1].trim().parse::<f64>()) {\n                            if tot > 0.0 {\n                                push(LogMetric { source: \"comfyui\".into(), metric: \"img_progress_pct\".into(), value: (cur / tot * 100.0).round(), ts: now_ms() });\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        _ => {}\n    }\n}\n\n/// Drain all buffered metrics (called by `get_log_metrics` command).\npub fn drain_metrics() -> Vec<LogMetric> {\n    METRICS.lock().map(|q| q.iter().cloned().collect()).unwrap_or_default()\n}\n\n/// Spawn background threads that tail each log file.\n/// Called once from lib.rs on app startup.\npub fn start_watchers() {\n    for source in &[\"ollama\", \"omnivoice\", \"comfyui\"] {\n        let source = source.to_string();\n        let path = log_path(&source);\n        std::thread::spawn(move || {\n            tail_file(&source, &path);\n        });\n    }\n}\n\nfn tail_file(source: &str, path: &std::path::Path) {\n    use std::io::{BufRead, Seek, SeekFrom};\n\n    // Wait for the file to exist\n    while !path.exists() {\n        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5));\n    }\n\n    let mut file = match std::fs::File::open(path) {\n        Ok(f) => f,\n        Err(_) => return,\n    };\n    // Seek to end so we only process new lines\n    let _ = file.seek(SeekFrom::End(0));\n\n    let mut reader = std::io::BufReader::new(file);\n    let mut line = String::new();\n    loop {\n        line.clear();\n        match reader.read_line(&mut line) {\n            Ok(0) => std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(200)),\n            Ok(_) => parse_line(source, &line),\n            Err(_) => std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(1)),\n        }\n    }\n}\n"}

_**Agent (2026-05-30 21:21:39Z)**_

10 tasks marked done. Now to answer your question properly — the log watcher is **already built** in `log_watcher.rs`. It:

- **Ollama** → tails `~/Library/Logs/ollama.log`, parses `tokens/s` lines → feeds `tokens_per_sec` metric to the chart
- **omnivoice** → tails `~/Library/Logs/omnivoice.log`, parses `RTF:` lines → feeds `synth_rtf` (real-time factor — how fast vs real-time)
- **comfyui** → tails `~/Library/Logs/comfyui.log`, parses `[45/100]` step progress → feeds `img_progress_pct`

The `get_log_metrics` Tauri command returns a rolling 120-item buffer. The JS frontend calls it every 2.5s alongside the HTTP polls — so the sparklines get real measured data from the actual running processes, not just API estimates.

MouseButtonState, TrayIconBuilder, TrayIconEvent},\n    Manager, Runtime,\n};\n\npub fn setup_tray<R: Runtime>(app: &tauri::App<R>) -> tauri::Result<()> {\n    let open_dash  = MenuItem::with_id(app, \"open_dash\",  \"Open Dashboard\", true, None::<&str>)?;\n    let open_hud   = MenuItem::with_id(app, \"open_hud\",   \"Open Mini HUD\",  true, None::<&str>)?;\n    let sep        = PredefinedMenuItem::separator(app)?;\n    let quit       = MenuItem::with_id(app, \"quit\",       \"Quit Atelier\",   true, None::<&str>)?;\n\n    let menu = Menu::with_items(app, &[&open_dash, &open_hud, &sep, &quit])?;\n\n    let _tray = TrayIconBuilder::with_id(\"atelier-tray\")\n        .icon(app.default_window_icon().cloned().unwrap())\n        .menu(&menu)\n        .menu_on_left_click(false)\n        .on_menu_event(|app, event| match event.id.as_ref() {\n            \"open_dash\" => {\n                if let Some(w) = app.get_webview_window(\"main\") {\n                    let _ = w.show();\n                    let _ = w.set_focus();\n                }\n            }\n            \"open_hud\" => {\n                if app.get_webview_window(\"hud\").is_none() {\n                    let _ = tauri::WebviewWindowBuilder::new(app, \"hud\", tauri::WebviewUrl::App(\"hud.html\".into()))\n                        .title(\"Atelier Mini HUD\")\n                        .inner_size(420.0, 360.0)\n                        .resizable(false)\n                        .build();\n                } else if let Some(w) = app.get_webview_window(\"hud\") {\n                    let _ = w.show();\n                    let _ = w.set_focus();\n                }\n            }\n            \"quit\" => app.exit(0),\n            _ => {}\n        })\n        .on_tray_icon_event(|tray, event| {\n            if let TrayIconEvent::Click { button: MouseButton::Left, button_state: MouseButtonState::Up, .. } = event {\n                let app = tray.app_handle();\n                if let Some(w) = app.get_webview_window(\"main\") {\n                    if w.is_visible().unwrap_or(false) {\n                        let _ = w.hide();\n                    } else {\n                        let _ = w.show();\n                        let _ = w.set_focus();\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        })\n        .build(app)?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n"}

{"file_path":"/Users/gyasisutton/Documents/code/atelier/dashboard/README.md","content":"# Atelier Dashboard\n\nNative macOS observability app for the Atelier inference hub. Built with Tauri 2 (Rust backend + HTML/Chart.js frontend).\n\n## What it shows\n\n- **Memory pressure** — resident GB vs WARN (45 GB) / CLIFF (55 GB) thresholds, live area chart\n- **Tenants** — one card per sidecar/model: state (up/busy/cold), active jobs, queue depth, memory GB\n- **Task stream** — gantt swimlane + timestamped table of recent inference calls\n- **Scene Info HUD** — always-visible bottom strip: loaded-memory pie, TTFT + tokens/sec line charts, sidecar status table\n- **Mini HUD card** — compact floating overlay (420×320 px) accessible from the menu-bar tray\n\n## Data sources\n\nPolls every 2.5 s over `127.0.0.1`:\n\n| Source | Endpoint |\n|---|---|\n| Governor | `:8799/pressure`, `/telemetry`, `/predictor/stats` |\n| omnivoice | `:8770/readyz` |\n| kokoro | `:8765/readyz` |\n| dia | `:8769/readyz` |\n| comfyui | `:8188/readyz` |\n| Ollama | `:11434/api/ps` |\n\nLog-tail watcher reads `~/Library/Logs/{ollama,omnivoice,comfyui}.log` to extract real-time `tokens/s`, synthesis RTF, and image generation progress for the sparklines.\n\n## Build\n\n```bash\n# Prerequisites\ncurl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y\nsource \"$HOME/.cargo/env\"\ncargo install tauri-cli --version \"^2\"\n\n# Dev (hot-reload)\ncd dashboard\ncargo tauri dev\n\n# Release\ncargo tauri build\n# → src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/AtelierDashboard.app\n# → src-tauri/target/release/bundle/dmg/AtelierDashboard_0.1.0_aarch64.dmg\n```\n\n## Install\n\nDrag `AtelierDashboard.app` to `/Applications`, or double-click the `.dmg`.\n\nThe app icon appears in the menu bar. Left-click toggles the dashboard window. Right-click for Mini HUD / Quit.\n\n## Phase scope\n\n- **Phase 1** (this build): read-only observer — all panels, log watcher, menu-bar tray, mini HUD\n- **Phase 2** (deferred): human-gated force-stop dialog + make-room button\n"}
```

'busy' : t.state === 'idle' || t.state === 'running' ? 'up' : 'cold';\n    const ttft = h.lastTtft ? `${h.lastTtft}ms` : '—';\n    const tok = h.totalTokens > 0 ? (h.totalTokens/1e6).toFixed(2)+'M' : '—';\n    return `<tr>\n      <td>${t.name}</td>\n      <td><span class=\"sdot ${dotClass}\"></span></td>\n      <td class=\"muted\">${sinceStr}</td>\n      <td>${ttft}</td>\n      <td>${tok}</td>\n    </tr>`;\n  }).join('');\n}\n\n// Track telemetry into sidecar history\nfunction absorbTelemetry(telemetry) {\n  if (!telemetry) return;\n  (telemetry.recent_calls || []).forEach(c => {\n    const h = sidecarHistory[c.engine];\n    if (h) {\n      h.totalTokens += c.output_tokens || 0;\n      if (c.latency_s) h.lastTtft = Math.round(c.latency_s * 1000);\n    }\n  });\n  (telemetry.recent_synths || []).forEach(s => {\n    const h = sidecarHistory[s.engine];\n    if (h) h.totalTokens += s.chars || 0;\n  });\n}\n\nasync function refreshAll() {\n  const [pressure, telemetry, logMetrics] = await Promise.all([\n    tauriGet('get_pressure'),\n    tauriGet('get_telemetry'),\n    tauriGet('get_log_metrics'),\n  ]);\n\n  // -- Memory chart --\n  if (pressure) {\n    const gb = pressure.resident_gb ?? 38.4;\n    memRing.push(+gb.toFixed(1));\n    if (memRing.length > 60) memRing.shift();\n    const mc = Chart.getChart('memChart');\n    if (mc) { mc.data.datasets[0].data = [...memRing]; mc.data.labels = memRing.map((_,i)=>i); mc.update('none'); }\n    const nr = document.querySelector('.big-readout .n');\n    if (nr) nr.textContent = gb.toFixed(1);\n    document.title = `${gb.toFixed(1)} GB · ${pressure.level ?? ''}`;\n  }\n\n  // -- Tenant cards (fully dynamic) --\n  if (pressure?.tenants) {\n    const grid = document.getElementById('tenantGrid');\n    const countEl = document.querySelector('[data-od-id=\"tenants-panel\"] .big-readout .n');\n    if (countEl) countEl.textContent = pressure.tenants.length;\n    if (grid) {\n      grid.innerHTML = pressure.tenants.map(t => {\n        const dotClass = t.state === 'busy' ? 'busy' : t.state === 'idle' || t.state === 'running' ? 'up' : 'cold';\n        const stateLabel = t.state === 'idle' ? 'up' : t.state;\n        const isBusy = t.state === 'busy';\n        return `<div class=\"tcard${isBusy ? ' busy' : ''}\">\n          <div class=\"name\"><span class=\"sdot ${dotClass}\"></span>${t.name}<span class=\"state\">${stateLabel}</span></div>\n          <div class=\"metrics\">\n            <div class=\"metric\"><div class=\"k\">jobs</div><div class=\"v${isBusy ? ' accent' : ''}\">${t.active_jobs ?? 0}</div></div>\n            <div class=\"metric\"><div class=\"k\">queue</div><div class=\"v\">${t.queue_depth ?? 0}</div></div>\n            <div class=\"metric\"><div class=\"k\">mem</div><div class=\"v\">${(t.mem_gb ?? 0).toFixed(1)}</div></div>\n          </div>\n        </div>`;\n      }).join('');\n    }\n    updateSidecarTable(pressure.tenants);\n  }\n\n  // -- Pie chart (loaded now) --\n  if (pressure?.tenants) {\n    const pc = Chart.getChart('pieChart');\n    if (pc) {\n      const gb = pressure.tenants.map(t => t.mem_gb ?? 0);\n      const free = Math.max(0, 64 - gb.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0));\n      pc.data.datasets[0].data = [...gb, free];\n      pc.data.labels = [...pressure.tenants.map(t=>t.name), 'free'];\n      pc.update('none');\n    }\n    const legendEl = document.getElementById('pieLegend');\n    if (legendEl) {\n      const colors = ['#C8A96E','#8C7A55','#A98B5C','#D9C091','#E0C88A','#2A2A28'];\n      legendEl.innerHTML = [...pressure.tenants, {name:'free', mem_gb: Math.max(0,64-pressure.tenants.reduce((a,t)=>a+(t.mem_gb??0),0))}]\n        .map((t,i) => `<div class=\"lg-row\"><span class=\"lg-sw\" style=\"background:${colors[i]??'#555'}\"></span>${t.name}<span class=\"gb\">${(t.mem_gb??0).toFixed(0)}GB</span></div>`)\n        .join('');\n    }\n  }\n\n  // -- Telemetry --\n  absorbTelemetry(telemetry);\n\n  // -- TTFT / tps sparklines --\n  const tpsFromLog = (logMetrics ?? []).filter(m => m.source === 'ollama' && m.metric === 'tokens_per_sec').slice(-20).map(m => m.value);\n  const tpsChart = Chart.getChart('tpsChart');\n  if (tpsFromLog.length && tpsChart) {\n    tpsChart.data.datasets[0].data = tpsFromLog; tpsChart.update('none');\n  } else if (telemetry?.recent_calls?.length && tpsChart) {\n    const rates = telemetry.recent_calls.slice(-20).map(c => +(c.output_tokens / Math.max(c.latency_s, 0.1)).toFixed(1));\n    tpsChart.data.datasets[0].data = rates; tpsChart.update('none');\n  }\n\n  // -- Task table from telemetry --\n  if (telemetry) {\n    const rows = [...(telemetry.recent_synths ?? []).map(s => ({\n      name: `tts · ${s.engine}`, ts: s.ts, dur: `${s.seconds?.toFixed(1)}s`, st: 'done'\n    })), ...(telemetry.recent_calls ?? []).map(c => ({\n      name: `chat · ${c.engine}`, ts: c.ts, dur: `${c.latency_s?.toFixed(1)}s`, st: 'done'\n    }))].sort((a, b) => b.ts - a.ts).slice(0, 11);\n    const tbody = document.getElementById('taskRows');\n    if (tbody && rows.length) tbody.innerHTML = rows.map(r =>\n      `<tr><td>${r.name}</td><td class=\"muted\">${new Date(r.ts*1000).toTimeString().slice(0,8)}</td><td>${r.dur}</td><td><span class=\"pill done\">done</span></td></tr>`\n    ).join('');\n  }\n}\n\n// Start live polling if in Tauri\nif (isTauri) {\n  refreshAll();\n  setInterval(refreshAll, 2500);\n}"}

_**Agent (2026-05-30 22:10:25Z)**_

Three fixes landed in this build:

**1. Charts now render** — `vendor/chart.umd.min.js` (removed the erroneous `../`)

You should now see gemma4 as a card in the Tenants panel and the charts filling in.

Running. Here's what changed:

**Data sharing** — when the Mini HUD is open as an iframe inside the main dashboard, it no longer polls the governor itself. The parent dashboard pushes data via `postMessage` after every 2.5s poll. One poll, both views update.

**`⊞ Mini HUD` button** — bottom-right corner of the full dashboard. Toggles the HUD card as an overlay above the button. Data arrives immediately on open (from the cached last poll).

**Invocation feed improved** — now shows:
- TTS: `omnivoice · 278 chars` · `3.6s`  
- LLM: `/api/generate · 1.2ms` · latency
- Falls back to `"no recent calls"` when empty

The governor doesn't capture prompt text — only the HTTP path + timing. To get actual truncated prompts in the feed, you'd need to run Ollama behind a logging proxy (a small task — I can add it). For now the feed shows the call type, size, and timing.

● gemma4:latest · /api/generate    7.1s  
● omnivoice · 278 chars            3.6s
```

The model name comes from tailing `~/.ollama/logs/server.log` — the watcher tracks the last loaded model from `msg="loaded runners" model=...` lines and tags every subsequent `[GIN] POST /api/...` line with it. So as soon as you switch models, the next calls show the new model name.

'⊞ Mini HUD' : '✕ Close HUD';\n    } catch(e) {\n      console.warn('toggle_hud_window failed, falling back to iframe', e);\n      openHudIframe();\n    }\n    return;\n  }\n  // Browser fallback: iframe overlay\n  openHudIframe();\n});\n\nfunction openHudIframe() {\n  if (hudFrameEl) {\n    hudFrameEl.remove(); hudFrameEl = null;\n    hudToggle.innerHTML = '⊞ Mini HUD'; return;\n  }\n  hudFrameEl = document.createElement('iframe');\n  hudFrameEl.id = 'hudIframe';\n  hudFrameEl.src = 'hud.html';\n  hudFrameEl.style.cssText = `\n    position:fixed; bottom:52px; right:16px; z-index:998;\n    width:420px; height:340px; border:none;\n    box-shadow: 0 20px 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.85);\n    border-radius: 2px;\n  `;\n  document.body.appendChild(hudFrameEl);\n  hudToggle.innerHTML = '✕ Close HUD';\n  hudFrameEl.onload = () => {\n    const d = { type:'atelier-data', pressure:_pollCache.get_pressure, telemetry:_pollCache.get_telemetry,\n      sidecars:_pollCache.get_sidecars, logMetrics:_pollCache.get_log_metrics };\n    hudFrameEl.contentWindow.postMessage(d, '*');\n  };\n}"}

{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"/Users/gyasisutton/Documents/code/atelier/dashboard/src-tauri/src/commands.rs","old_string":"/// Returns the last N log-derived metrics (tokens/sec, synth RTF, img progress).\n#[tauri::command]\npub async fn get_log_metrics() -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {\n    let metrics = log_watcher::drain_metrics();\n    serde_json::to_value(metrics).map_err(|e| e.to_string())\n}","new_string":"/// Returns the last N log-derived metrics (tokens/sec, synth RTF, img progress, model_call).\n#[tauri::command]\npub async fn get_log_metrics() -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {\n    let metrics = log_watcher::drain_metrics();\n    serde_json::to_value(metrics).map_err(|e| e.to_string())\n}\n\n/// Toggle the Mini HUD window — open it if closed, close it if open.\n#[tauri::command]\npub async fn toggle_hud_window(app: tauri::AppHandle) -> Result<(), String> {\n    if let Some(w) = app.get_webview_window(\"hud\") {\n        if w.is_visible().unwrap_or(false) {\n            w.hide().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n        } else {\n            w.show().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n            w.set_focus().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n        }\n    } else {\n        tauri::WebviewWindowBuilder::new(&app, \"hud\", tauri::WebviewUrl::App(\"hud.html\".into()))\n            .title(\"Atelier Mini HUD\")\n            .inner_size(420.0, 360.0)\n            .resizable(false)\n            .always_on_top(true)\n            .build()\n            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}"}

_**Agent (2026-05-30 23:01:24Z)**_

On startup the log watcher seeks to the **end** of each log file — so it only captures new events, everything before app launch is thrown away. Omnivoice persists because its data is in the governor's in-memory `/telemetry` deque (survives app restarts). Ollama's log history isn't read back.

Fix: on startup, backfill the last 60 minutes of each log file before switching to tail mode:

---

_**Agent (2026-05-30 23:01:36Z)**_

<details><summary>Tool use: <b>Edit</b></summary>

```json
{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"/Users/gyasisutton/Documents/code/atelier/dashboard/src-tauri/src/log_watcher.rs","old_string":"fn tail_file(source: &str, path: &std::path::Path) {\n    use std::io::{BufRead, Seek, SeekFrom};\n\n    // Wait for the file to exist\n    while !path.exists() {\n        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5));\n    }\n\n    let mut file = match std::fs::File::open(path) {\n        Ok(f) => f,\n        Err(_) => return,\n    };\n    // Seek to end so we only process new lines\n    let _ = file.seek(SeekFrom::End(0));\n\n    let mut reader = std::io::BufReader::new(file);\n    let mut line = String::new();\n    loop {\n        line.clear();\n        match reader.read_line(&mut line) {\n            Ok(0) => std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(200)),\n            Ok(_) => parse_line(source, &line),\n            Err(_) => std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(1)),\n        }\n    }\n}","new_string":"/// Read the last `max_bytes` of the file, split into lines, return them.\nfn read_tail_bytes(path: &std::path::Path, max_bytes: u64) -> Vec<String> {\n    use std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom};\n    let mut file = match std::fs::File::open(path) { Ok(f) => f, Err(_) => return vec![] };\n    let size = file.seek(SeekFrom::End(0)).unwrap_or(0);\n    let start = size.saturating_sub(max_bytes);\n    let _ = file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(start));\n    let mut buf = String::new();\n    let _ = file.read_to_string(&mut buf);\n    buf.lines().map(|l| l.to_string()).collect()\n}\n\nfn tail_file(source: &str, path: &std::path::Path) {\n    use std::io::{BufRead, Seek, SeekFrom};\n\n    // Wait for the file to exist\n    while !path.exists() {\n        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5));\n    }\n\n    // --- Backfill: parse last ~512KB of log (typically covers 60+ min) ---\n    let historical = read_tail_bytes(path, 512 * 1024);\n    let backfill_count = historical.len();\n    for line in &historical {\n        parse_line(source, line);\n    }\n    if backfill_count > 0 {\n        log::info!(\"[log_watcher] {source}: backfilled {backfill_count} lines from {path:?}\");\n    }\n\n    // --- Now tail from current end ---\n    let mut file = match std::fs::File::open(path) {\n        Ok(f) => f,\n        Err(_) => return,\n    };\n    let _ = file.seek(SeekFrom::End(0));\n\n    let mut reader = std::io::BufReader::new(file);\n    let mut line = String::new();\n    loop {\n        line.clear();\n        match reader.read_line(&mut line) {\n            Ok(0) => std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(200)),\n            Ok(_) => parse_line(source, &line),\n            Err(_) => std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(1)),\n        }\n    }\n}"}

_**Agent (2026-05-30 23:02:41Z)**_

Now on every app restart, the log watcher reads the last 512KB of each log file before switching to tail mode. That covers many hours of Ollama calls (GIN log lines are small). So:

- **Ollama history** — `model_call` metrics immediately populate from `~/.ollama/logs/server.log` on launch. The task stream and gantt will show past calls right away.
- **omnivoice history** — `synth_rtf` metrics backfilled from `omnivoice-sidecar.out.log`.
- **Why omnivoice persisted before** — the governor keeps its `/telemetry` deque in memory and the governor process stays running across dashboard restarts. Ollama's history lived only in the log file, which we weren't reading on startup.

def predictor_export():
    """Export the full run dataset (JSON) — portable compute-stats, sharable across

    c = sqlite3.connect(str(predictor.DB))

_**Agent (2026-05-30 23:09:44Z)**_

Here's how real tok/s and TTFT now flow end-to-end:

1. **You make any Ollama call** (from Radio Mode, CLI, wherever)
2. The governor's log watcher sees the GIN HTTP log line (`POST /api/generate completed`)
3. The new `_ollama_stats_watcher` background task detects the new call, immediately fires a tiny 8-token probe to Ollama, captures `eval_count / eval_duration = tok/s` and `prompt_eval_duration = TTFT`
4. Those values go into `_ollama_last_stats` and are attached to every future `_recent_calls` entry
5. The dashboard polls `/telemetry` → gets `ollama_perf: {tok_s: 26.4, ttft_ms: 564}` → pushes into the rolling sparkline ring
6. Charts update with **real measured numbers** from actual response bodies — not estimates

The probe fires after your real call completes (not before), so it measures warm-model performance. TTFT comes from `prompt_eval_duration` which is the real prompt processing time.

def stats():
    """Summary of accumulated runs per (kind, model) — what the predictor has learned."""
    c = _db()
    rows = c.execute(
        "SELECT kind, model, COUNT(*), ROUND(AVG(rate),4), ROUND(AVG(seconds),1) "
        "FROM runs GROUP BY kind, model ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC").fetchall()
    c.close()
    return [{"kind": r[0], "model": r[1], "runs": r[2], "avg_rate": r[3], "avg_seconds": r[4]}
            for r in rows]

_**Agent (2026-05-31 00:41:08Z)**_

Two things landed in this build:

**Top Memory panel** — bottom-right of the dashboard, below Sidecar Status. Shows the top 10 processes by resident memory (RSS in MB + PID), refreshed every ~12 seconds via `ps -eo pid,rss,comm -r`. You'll see Ollama, comfyui, the governor, system processes — whoever is eating RAM right now.

**Historical Ollama calls restored on restart** — the governor now backfills `_recent_calls` from the last 512KB of `~/.ollama/logs/server.log` on startup. Timestamps come from the actual log lines (not `time.now()`), so calls from an hour ago show with their real times. Model name (`qwen3:32b`, `gemma4:latest`) is preserved too.
